name: Six Sigma Green Belt
tagline: Process improvement certification for project leads using DMAIC
about: Six Sigma Green Belt validates the ability to lead small-scale process improvement projects using the DMAIC framework (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control). Topics include statistical process control, hypothesis testing, design of experiments, lean tools, root cause analysis, and project management. Two main certifying bodies exist: ASQ's Certified Six Sigma Green Belt (CSSGB) and IASSC's ICGB. Used across manufacturing, healthcare, financial services, and IT operations to qualify analysts and team leads for process improvement work, often a stepping stone to Six Sigma Black Belt.

name: Project Management Professional (PMP)
tagline: The flagship project management certification
about: PMP validates skills in leading projects across predictive (waterfall), agile, and hybrid approaches. Covers people, process, and business environment domains. Required or preferred for many senior project manager and program manager roles across industries.

name: A&P (Airframe and Powerplant) Mechanic
tagline: FAA certification for aircraft maintenance technicians
about: A&P certification covers airframe structures, systems, powerplant theory, inspection, and FAA regulations. Required for performing or signing off most airline and general-aviation maintenance work in the United States.

name: Medical Billing and Coding (CPC / CCS)
tagline: Healthcare reimbursement, ICD-10, CPT, and HCPCS coding
about: Medical Billing and Coding certifications (CPC from AAPC, CCS from AHIMA) cover ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes, CPT procedure codes, HCPCS Level II codes, anatomy, medical terminology, payer rules, and the revenue cycle. High-demand role with strong remote-work options.

name: Insurance Producer License
tagline: State licenses for selling life, health, and property/casualty insurance
about: Insurance Producer licensing covers insurance principles, policy types, regulations, ethics, and state-specific law for life, health, and property and casualty lines. Required by every state for selling, soliciting, or negotiating insurance products.

name: Systems Security Certified Practitioner (SSCP)
tagline: ISC2's entry-level cybersecurity certification — the operational counterpart to CISSP
about: SSCP from ISC2 is the entry-level technical certification for IT administrators, security operations staff, and analysts who implement and monitor security controls day-to-day. The exam covers seven domains: Security Operations and Administration, Access Controls, Risk Identification & Monitoring & Analysis, Incident Response and Recovery, Cryptography, Network and Communications Security, and Systems and Application Security. Format: 125 multiple-choice questions, 3 hours, $249. Requires 1 year of paid work experience in one or more of the seven domains. Often described as the operational/hands-on counterpart to the more strategic CISSP.

name: FAA Private Pilot Certificate
tagline: Foundational pilot certificate for personal flight
about: Private Pilot Certificate covers regulations, navigation, weather, aerodynamics, aircraft systems, performance and weight balance, and emergency procedures. Required for piloting most personal single-engine aircraft and a stepping stone toward commercial pilot training.

name: Electrician License (Apprentice / Journeyman / Master)
tagline: State-licensed credential for residential and commercial electrical work
about: Electrician licensing covers the National Electrical Code (NEC), wiring methods, conductor sizing, overcurrent protection, grounding and bonding, motors, transformers, hazardous locations, and safety. Licensed at apprentice, journeyman, and master levels by state regulators.

name: Plumbing License (Apprentice / Journeyman / Master)
tagline: State-licensed credential for plumbing system installation and repair
about: Plumbing licensing covers code (UPC or IPC), drain-waste-vent systems, water supply, fixture installation, gas piping, backflow prevention, and trade safety. Licensed at apprentice, journeyman, and master levels by state regulators.

name: Certified Medical Assistant (CMA)
tagline: Clinical and administrative support for medical practices
about: Medical Assistant certifications (CMA, RMA, CCMA) cover clinical procedures, medical terminology, anatomy, phlebotomy basics, EKG, vital signs, medication administration, and front-office tasks like scheduling, insurance, and EHR documentation.

name: AWS Certified Welder
tagline: Performance-based certification for production welders
about: AWS Certified Welder is a performance-based credential confirming a welder can produce sound welds to a specified procedure on a specified material and process. Widely accepted across construction, manufacturing, pipeline, and shipbuilding industries.

name: SHRM Certified Professional (SHRM-CP)
tagline: Society for Human Resource Management early-career HR credential
about: SHRM-CP is the entry-level certification from the Society for Human Resource Management, designed for HR professionals who implement policies and serve as the point of contact for employees and managers. The exam tests competencies (leadership, ethical practice, business acumen, relationship management, consultation, critical evaluation, global mindset, communication) and HR knowledge across people, organization, workplace, and strategy. Format: 134 questions (knowledge-based + situational-judgment items), 4 hours. A senior-level companion credential (SHRM-SCP) is available for HR managers and directors.

name: Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM)
tagline: PMI's entry-level project management certification
about: CAPM is PMI's entry-level credential for new project coordinators and team members. The exam covers predictive (plan-driven) project management, agile frameworks, business analysis, and the project life cycle. CAPM has no work-experience requirement (unlike PMP) but does require 23 contact hours of project management education, satisfied by PMI's free CAPM Exam Prep course. Test format: 150 multiple-choice questions, 3 hours, computer-based.

name: Google Project Management Certificate
tagline: Coursera-based entry-level project management credential
about: The Google Project Management Certificate is a self-paced, course-based credential delivered through Coursera. Unlike PMP, it has no single proctored exam — instead, you complete six courses (foundations of project management, agile, capstone, etc.) with module quizzes and applied projects scored inside Coursera. It is designed for career-switchers and entry-level project coordinators, and counts for 100+ contact hours that can later be applied toward the PMP eligibility requirement.

name: Google IT Support Professional Certificate
tagline: Coursera-based entry-level IT support credential
about: The Google IT Support Professional Certificate is a self-paced, course-based credential delivered through Coursera. It covers technical support fundamentals, computer networking, operating systems, system administration, IT security, and customer-service skills across five courses. Unlike CompTIA A+ or Network+, there is no centralized proctored exam — completion is based on graded assignments and module quizzes inside Coursera. Designed for career-switchers and people targeting help desk, technical support, and IT support specialist roles.

name: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
tagline: Coursera-based entry-level data analytics credential
about: The Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate is a self-paced, course-based credential delivered through Coursera across eight courses. It covers the data analysis process, spreadsheets, SQL, R programming, Tableau, and data visualization. Like other Google career certificates, there is no centralized proctored exam — completion is based on graded assignments and quizzes inside Coursera. Targeted at career-switchers entering junior data analyst and BI analyst roles.

name: Google UX Design Professional Certificate
tagline: Coursera-based entry-level UX design credential
about: The Google UX Design Professional Certificate is a self-paced, course-based credential delivered through Coursera. It covers the UX design process, user research, wireframing, low-fidelity prototyping, high-fidelity prototyping in Figma and Adobe XD, accessibility, and portfolio building. Completion is based on graded design exercises and module quizzes; there is no centralized proctored exam. Aimed at career-switchers targeting junior UX/UI designer roles.

name: Cosmetology Instructor License
tagline: State credential to teach cosmetology in licensed schools
about: Cosmetology Instructor licensing authorizes teaching cosmetology, barber, nail tech, and esthetics in state-licensed schools. Typically requires existing cosmetology license, instructor training hours, and an instructor-specific exam covering pedagogy and student-clinic supervision.

name: Salon and Shop Manager License
tagline: State license to manage cosmetology, barber, and nail salons
about: Salon Manager licensing authorizes overseeing operations and licensed staff in beauty establishments. Required in some states for anyone managing a licensed salon. Covers sanitation regulations, infection control, recordkeeping, and state-specific salon law.

name: Combined Esthetics and Nail Technology License
tagline: Esthetics plus Nail Technology in one credential
about: Combined Practice licenses cover both esthetics (skin care, hair removal, makeup) and nail technology under one credential. Available in states that allow combined exams to reduce duplication of training hours.

name: Advanced Esthetics License
tagline: Medical-grade skin procedures for advanced-practice estheticians
about: Advanced Esthetics extends the standard Esthetician license with chemical peels, microneedling, advanced exfoliation, microdermabrasion, and laser/IPL hair removal. Required in some states for med-spa work and esthetic-clinic employment.

name: Electrology License (Permanent Hair Removal)
tagline: State license for permanent hair removal with an electric needle
about: Electrology is permanent hair removal using a fine probe to deliver an electric current to individual hair follicles. State licensing covers anatomy, electrology theory, electrolysis vs. thermolysis vs. blend modalities, sterilization, and clinical practice.

name: Hair Removal Specialty License
tagline: State license for waxing, sugaring, and threading
about: Hair Removal specialty licenses authorize waxing, sugaring, threading, and basic depilatory services. Excludes electrology and laser hair removal. Lower hour requirement than full Esthetician — popular for waxing-only studios.

name: Hair Designer License
tagline: Cutting and styling specialty without chemical services
about: Hair Designer covers hair cutting, blow-out, thermal styling, and braiding without chemical services. Reduced hour requirements compared to full Cosmetology, often used as a stepping stone or specialization.

name: Natural Hair Styling and Braiding License
tagline: Braiding and natural hair specialty (no chemicals)
about: Natural Hair Styling covers braiding, locking, twisting, and natural hair care without chemical services. Required in many states for braiders; reduced-hour alternative to full Cosmetology and a key license for protective-style specialists.

name: Blow Dry Styling License
tagline: Limited license for blow-out salons (no cutting, no chemicals)
about: Blow Dry Styling licenses authorize shampooing, conditioning, blow-drying, thermal styling, and basic dry styling. No cutting and no chemical services. Designed for blow-dry-bar employees in states that recognize this reduced-scope credential.

name: Barber Styling License
tagline: Barber and limited cosmetology hybrid for chemical hair services
about: Barber Styling combines barber services with chemical hair services (color, perms, relaxers) for male and female clientele. Available in states that recognize a hybrid scope between Barber and Cosmetology.

name: EMT (Emergency Medical Technician)
tagline: Entry-level certification for emergency medical services
about: EMT certification covers patient assessment, airway management, trauma care, medical emergencies, pharmacology, and ambulance operations. Required by most states for ambulance and emergency response roles, validated through NREMT cognitive and psychomotor exams.

name: Certified Phlebotomy Technician (CPT)
tagline: Specialized blood-draw certification for clinical labs
about: CPT certification covers venipuncture, capillary collection, specimen handling, patient identification, infection control, anatomy of the circulatory system, and clinical lab procedures. A short-program credential commonly used as an entry point into healthcare.

name: Nail Technology License
tagline: State license for manicures, pedicures, and nail enhancements
about: Nail Technology licensing covers manicures, pedicures, acrylic and gel enhancements, dip powder, nail art, sanitation, and anatomy of the hand and foot. Standalone specialty license in most states, often combined with esthetics.

name: Eyelash and Eyebrow Technician License
tagline: Specialty license for lash extensions, lifts, tinting, and brow services
about: Eyelash and Eyebrow Technician licenses cover classic and volume lash extensions, lash lifts, tinting, brow waxing and tinting, and brow lamination. Lower hour requirement than full Esthetician — popular as a focused career path.

name: Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA)
tagline: Entry point into the nursing and long-term care field
about: CNA covers basic nursing skills, infection control, vital signs, communication, residents' rights, and personal care. Required for working in nursing homes and long-term care under federal OBRA regulations and tested via state competency exams.

name: Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I)
tagline: Scrum.org's entry-level Scrum Master certification
about: PSM I from Scrum.org validates your understanding of Scrum as defined by the Scrum Guide. The 60-minute, 80-question online exam tests your knowledge of Scrum theory, the Scrum Team, Scrum events, Scrum artifacts, and Done. No mandatory training is required — you can take the exam directly for $200. PSM I does not expire (one-time fee, lifetime credential), which sets it apart from the rival CSM (Certified ScrumMaster) from Scrum Alliance, which requires renewal.

name: ServSafe Food Protection Manager
tagline: ANSI-accredited manager-level food safety certification
about: ServSafe Food Protection Manager certification covers foodborne illness, the flow of food, food safety management systems, sanitary facilities and equipment, regulatory authorities, and crisis management. Accepted by jurisdictions nationwide as the food protection manager certification.

name: Permanent Makeup License
tagline: Cosmetic-tattoo license for brows, eyeliner, and lips
about: Permanent Makeup is cosmetic tattooing of brows (microblading, powder, ombré), eyeliner, lip color, and beauty-mark restoration. In some states this is a distinct license from Micropigmentation; in others they're combined. Requires bloodborne pathogen, sterilization, and infection-control training.

name: Ear Piercing Specialty License
tagline: Limited license for ear-only piercing
about: Ear Piercing licenses authorize ear-lobe (and sometimes cartilage) piercing in salons, mall kiosks, and retail. Lower training hours than full Body Piercing because of the limited scope. Required in many states even at retail jewelry stores.

name: ASE Automotive Certification
tagline: Industry-standard certification for automotive technicians
about: ASE Automotive certifications cover engine repair, transmission, drivetrain, suspension and steering, brakes, electrical systems, HVAC, engine performance, light-duty diesel, and maintenance and light repair. Most automotive repair shops prefer or require ASE-certified technicians.

name: EPA 608 Refrigerant Handling Certification
tagline: Federal certification required to handle HVAC refrigerants
about: EPA 608 covers ozone depletion, the Clean Air Act, refrigerant recovery and recycling, leak detection, safety, and shipping for stationary refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment. Required under EPA Section 608 for purchasing or servicing equipment containing regulated refrigerants.

name: ServSafe Food Handler
tagline: Entry-level food safety certification for restaurant workers
about: ServSafe Food Handler covers basic food safety, personal hygiene, cross-contamination, time and temperature control, cleaning and sanitizing, and allergen awareness. Required by many state and local jurisdictions for anyone handling food in restaurants.

name: Esthetician License
tagline: State-licensed credential for professional skin care services
about: The Esthetician License is required in every U.S. state to perform professional skin care services for compensation — facials, hair removal, makeup, skin analysis, chemical exfoliation, and body treatments. State exams typically follow the NIC National Esthetics Theory blueprint, covering scientific concepts (infection control, anatomy and physiology, skin analysis, chemistry), esthetic services (consultation, facials, hair removal, makeup, body treatments), and the implements, tools, and equipment used in the skin care studio.

name: Body Piercing License
tagline: State-licensed credential for body piercing, sterilization, anatomy, jewelry, and safe procedure technique
about: A Body Piercing License authorizes piercing of the ear cartilage, nose, lip, tongue, navel, nipple, and other body sites for compensation. Most states use the NIC (National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology) National Body Piercing Theory Examination, a 110-item (100 weighted), 90-minute written exam, paired with a hands-on practical. The theory blueprint covers two domains: scientific concepts (microbiology, infection control levels and methods, Standard Precautions, blood exposure and needle-stick procedures, anatomy and physiology, skin histology, anomalies and disorders, jewelry materials, 55%) and piercing procedures and services (client consultation and consent, outcomes and complications, tools and equipment, jewelry suitability, skin prep and placement marking, piercing technique, jewelry changes and stretching, aftercare, 45%). References include Milady, the APP Procedure Manual, the Body Art Model Code, and The Piercing Bible.
